fields.h1: Build a Trivia Quiz That Keeps Score for You
fields.hero_description: Build a trivia quiz that scores every answer, ranks teams after each round, and saves results to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Inside a Trivia Quiz Built on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: Each trivia question has one right answer. Emergent builds the questions, the scoring, and the table that keeps every result.
fields.feature_1:
Rounds drafted around your topics

Name the rounds you want, such as science or 1990s music, and Emergent drafts 5 questions for each with 4 answer choices. Check every answer, then change any question by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Standings after every round

The app adds up each team's points when a round closes and puts the standings on the bar TV or the projector. Every team knows its place before the next round begins.
fields.feature_3:
A clock on each question

Set a limit per question, such as 30 seconds, and the app locks answers when it runs out. Every team gets the same window, and a late answer scores nothing for anyone.
fields.feature_4:
One question per screen on a phone

Players answer on their phones, one question per screen. A team can share one phone or each player can answer alone, and Emergent sets no cap on how many people play.
fields.feature_5:
Every answer saved to your database

Each answer is a row in a database you own, with the player, the round, and the seconds taken. Sort by question to find the ones half the room missed, and replace them.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and the full code

Run the quiz on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it after the season.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Hosts Run a Trivia Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
The Fact Hounds beat 10 teams with 27 of 30

Every Tuesday, 11 teams at Tidewater Tap play 6 rounds of 5 questions, one phone per team. After each round, the app totals the points and the bar TV shows the new order. Last week The Fact Hounds finished on 27 of 30, with Last Call Scholars second on 25.
fields.tab_content_2:
51 of 84 students miss one moon-phase question

On Fridays, 84 students in 3 science classes at Pinecrest Ridge Middle School take a 12-question review on their phones. The app flags any question missed by more than half of them. This week only the moon-phase question crossed that line, missed by 51 of 84, and it opens Monday's lesson.
fields.tab_content_3:
Omaha tops two other offices with an 11.4 average

Once a month, Calloway Freight runs a 15-question lunch quiz for 62 staff in Denver, Omaha, and Tulsa. Each office scores the average of its players, and a bigger office gets no head start. In March, Omaha's 17 players averaged 11.4 out of 15, and the app posted the win to the company Slack channel.
fields.tab_content_4:
A tie at 34 settled by one closest guess

The Maple Hollow Library fills its fall trivia night with 18 teams and 40 questions in 4 rounds. Shelf Awareness and the Barrowby Readers tied at 34. The tiebreaker asked how many books the library lent last year, and the answer was 61,240. Shelf Awareness guessed 58,000, closer than 52,500, and took first place.
